I'm looking at getting a reliable and powerful pistol to accompany me on my ranch and while hiking in the US south west. Due to the nature of the area, I would prefer to have a specific pistol for this as my EDC single stack 9mm likely wouldn't be as good of an option.

I can't quite decide what would be best for the area. There are javelina, coyotes, wild burros, rattle snakes, scorpions, bears and mountain lions in the area. My ranch land isn't habited yet by people and never has been, it's very secluded and there are already wildlife living on it that has shown to be territorial (I had wild burros huffing/puffing at me but I kept my distance and let them be). I've found coyote tracks in the mud as well. Under any given rock formation or in the shade could lurk a rattle snake as well.

I have been leaning towards the Taurus Judge as I like the idea of shooting .410 shot shells as I fear the rattle snakes more than anything else. If I am around my immediate living area I will, uh, take care of the snake. Using some snake or bird shot in a .410 shell makes it easier to hit. Would also work on scorpions and would hopefully deter anything else brave enough to pose a threat, but wouldn't be powerful enough to do anything than piss off a larger animal... (But I can still load 45 long colts with the Judge as well)

Alternatively I was thinking about 44 magnum revolver. This would be a powerful enough load to take out a javelina and a scrawny/hungry desert bear (hopefully)... and with proper aim could of course be used as a snake gun as well.

I've also considered a full size Glock 10mm... Glock 20 or even the longer Glock 40 would offer a powerful round and give me much more capacity than a wheel gun...

I'll be honest, my main concern are snakes because it's much more likely I'll encounter a rattler than I would a mountain lion or bear near me so I am leaning towards the Judge / SW Govenor (can shoot 45ACP from the Govenor as well as 410 / 45LC) but IDK. I've got rifles and shotguns and other pistols as well. Coyotes likely won't be a face to face problem and can be picked off with the AR or Mosin. The wild burros are probably harmless but they'll stomp a dog to death and would probably try to do the same to me if I got too close. They like to hang around an area where I'll be building though. I am sure they will move away after my presence is more profound in that area.

Unfortunately I don't have the means to test these out before deciding.

What would you recommend for such a situation?
Ranch / Hiking pistol recommendations for the US south west?

The Judge has QC problems and doesn't function very well as a .45 colt revolver. The Governor is a better gun but it's still huge and not as great as a revolver.

Ruger recently came out with a .45 Colt Redhawk so you can get a double action revolver that can shoot light cowboy target all the way to .44 Magnum Power loads. Snakes you say? There are .45 colt shotshells that work just fine. You don't need a .410 shotshell.

Single actions are a bit cheaper so you can get a Blackhawk .45 Colt convertible that will also do .45 acp.

EDIT: also because I'm an Idiot I forgot to tell you that the new Redhawk is cut for moon clips so you can shoot .45acp. Great for plinking, competitions and even some carry situations where you don't want full .45 colt (or the acp loads had better availability)

The new Redhawk is nice and I was lusting after it (for the same reason as OP), but the price made me reconcider. The new S&W 625 is pricey too. I think I'm going to get a used S&W Model 22-4 or maybe a Model 1955 or other moonclip gun. A Charter Pitbull in .45 would be great too, but it's a rarity. The Pitbull is much lighter than Redhawk (or a Smith actually), so I'll keep an eye out for one, but it's not likely. The 22-4 is the people's gun for this kind of thing. Sadly I'm not that good with SA and if I run across a snake it may matter, so I'm not considering a Vaquero or such.
Glock for sure. High caliber plus capacity is a win win situation.
Is there a snake shot load in 10mm? Also, would a G20 be okay in the dust of the trail without cleaning it every night?
Yes there is. Glocks don't jam unless you limp wrist.

The .410 revolvers are very bulky and heavy and they would only really excel as snake killers. For everything else they would be a compromise.

I don't have a ton of outdoors experience, but what little I do have has taught me that weight and bulk are not your friends. A four-inch barreled S&W .44 mag mountain gun, one of their new .44 mag L-frames, or a .44 or .45 blackhawk single action will carry much more nicely and do everything you need - the first round up can be a shotshell, if you like. With a four inch barrel, I don't think any of these would exceed the weight of a fully loaded full-sized glock.

The glock is a good second choice, the only drawback is that I don't think shotshells are available for it. It does have the advantage of being flatter, and arguably more resistant to abuse.

Another advantage to the revolvers is that a wide variety of grips are available, and the better they fit your hand, the better you'll shoot them. They can also accept a wide variety of ammunition, allowing you to select the power level you prefer.

You might consider a lanyard, too. A full-flap holster might be a good idea as well.

My ranch pistol is a Ruger Blackhawk in .44 mag. w/ 4.2" barrel. I carry one extra speed loader. .44 mag will handle just about any situation. Not sure about CCI snake shot - never tried it. I have shot quite a few snakes with normal loads.

I like Glocks and have owned several. My EDC is a Glock 36. The 10mm Glock sounds like a viable alternative to a large caliber revolver. Ammo is pretty expensive. Not sure they make 10mm snake shot. I would not be using those loads in a semi-auto anyway.

I would recommend the Smith & Wesson Governor. I use mine as my bedside gun and always felt that its home would be out in the woods or fields. Two .410 000 buckshot, two .45 Colt, and two .410 birdshot will get you through both large and small predators and pests.
